title: NJ BLS protocol map: what the EMT does under each
body:
Source: **New Jersey EMS Clinical Practice Protocols and Guidelines, version 1, effective 8/21/2025**, NJ Department of Health, Office of Emergency Medical Services. https://www.nj.gov/health/ems/documents/NEWJERSEYEMSCLINICALPRACTICEPROTOCOLS_GUIDELINES_FINAL8.21.2025v1.pdf

This index lists protocol numbers exactly as the 2025 document numbers them and summarizes only the steps printed under the **EMT** heading. Steps under Paramedic, MICN or Communication Failure are noted only where an EMT needs to anticipate them. Where the document does not state a number, this sheet says so rather than supplying one.

## How to read a NJ protocol

- Section 1 General Patient Care, 2 Medical, 3 Cardiac, 4 Trauma, 5 Airway, 6 Medical Procedures, 7 Prerequisite, 8 Medical Policies, 9 Hazmat and MCI.
- Suffix `A` is the adult version, `P` the pediatric version. No suffix means both.
- Headings inside each protocol run EMT, then PARAMEDIC & MICN, then COMMUNICATION FAILURE.
- Standing orders are cumulative. A medical director may **restrict, but not expand**, scope.
- "Call for ALS intercept" marks a point where a paramedic adds capability. Several protocols also say do not delay transport for it.

## Section 1 and 8: the rules that apply to every call

| Protocol | Title | What the EMT does |
|---|---|---|
| 1.0 | Routine Patient Care | Scene safety and standard precautions, count patients, determine MOI or nature of illness, control exsanguinating hemorrhage first, check whether DNR/POLST applies, check whether pediatric protocols apply, primary assessment, vitals every `15 min` if stable and every `5 min` if unstable, spinal assessment, destination and notification |
| 1.2 | Communication Failure Guidelines | Applies to ALS. EMTs should know it exists |
| 1.3 | Crashing Medical Patient in Extremis | Recognize and escalate early |
| 8.0 | Abuse & Neglect: Child, Elder, Human Trafficking | Recognize red flags, get the patient out of danger, do not confront the suspected perpetrator, report directly |
| 8.1 | Air Medical Transport | Determine need based on acuity and ground transport estimate |
| 8.2 | Trauma Triage & Transport Decision | Apply the National Guideline for the Field Triage of Injured Patients, RED and YELLOW criteria |
| 8.3 | Consent for Treatment of a Minor | Implied consent when a guardian is unavailable; telephonic parental refusal acceptable if documented |
| 8.4 | POLST | Four-step validity sequence; follow valid orders as written |
| 8.6 | Pediatric Transportation | Child-appropriate restraint and destination |
| 8.7 | Resuscitation Initiation & Termination | Check for a valid DNR before starting |
| 8.8 | Baby Safe Haven | Accept the infant, preserve anonymity, call `1-877-839-2339` by the next business day |

## Section 2: medical protocols with real EMT content

| Protocol | Title | EMT steps |
|---|---|---|
| 2.2 | Allergic Reaction / Anaphylaxis Adult | Allergic reaction: oxygen as needed, do not delay transport, consider ALS. Anaphylaxis: adult epinephrine auto-injector `0.3 mg IM`, anterolateral thigh preferred; repeat dosing needs medical command; do not delay transport |
| 2.2P | Anaphylaxis Pediatric | Age and weight appropriate `0.15 mg` auto-injector; oxygen; maintain body temperature; encourage transport |
| 2.3A | Altered Mental Status Adult | Oxygen to `94%`; if severely depressed mentation and respirations with suspected opioid: BVM with `100%` oxygen plus NPA, then naloxone nasal spray `4 mg` in one nostril **or** `1 mg` per nostril by atomizer to max `4 mg`, repeat once after `5 min`; check glucose; stroke assessment; transport after naloxone |
| 2.5 | Asthma / COPD / RAD Adult | Position of comfort, saturation `94%` (`90%` in COPD), albuterol `2.5 mg` nebulized every `5 min` to max `3 doses` (agency must be approved) or assist the patient's MDI, CPAP with PEEP `5 mmHg` if worsening or severe |
| 2.8A | Diabetic Emergency, Hypoglycemia Adult | Glucose by glucometer if agency approved, oral glucose `1-2` tubes if alert enough to swallow and protect airway, have the patient or family stop an insulin pump if GCS under `15` |
| 2.8P | Hypoglycemia Pediatric | Oral glucose `0.5 g/kg` with the same alertness requirement |
| 2.23 | Stroke, Adult & Pediatric | B.E. F.A.S.T.; if positive run R.A.C.E.; score above `5` consider a Comprehensive Stroke Center per local protocol; notify "Stroke Alert and Time Last Known Well"; oxygen to `94-99%`; glucose check if approved; head of stretcher `30 degrees`; minimize scene time; do not delay for ALS |

> **Trap:** Behavioral emergencies (protocol 2.6, listed in the 2025 table of contents as Behavioral Emergencies including Suicide Attempts & Threats) is written for EMT, Paramedic and MICN together. Its key EMT line: a patient who is a danger to self or others may not refuse care.

## Section 3: cardiac

| Protocol | Title | EMT steps |
|---|---|---|
| 3.0 | Acute Coronary Syndrome Adult | Oxygen **only** for dyspnea, `SpO2` under `94%`, or heart failure signs; aspirin `324 mg` PO chewable; facilitate the patient's own nitroglycerin every `3-5 min` while symptoms persist and systolic stays at or above `100 mmHg`, max `3` doses; call ALS; if ALS unavailable and transport exceeds `10 minutes`, go to an interventional cath-capable hospital |
| 3.2A / 3.2P | Cardiac Arrest Adult / Pediatric | CPR and AED per current AHA sequence, airway management, check DNR/POLST first |
| 3.3 | Congestive Heart Failure (Pulmonary Edema) Adult | Upright positioning, oxygen to target, CPAP where the agency is approved |

## Section 4 and 5: trauma and airway

| Protocol | Title | EMT steps |
|---|---|---|
| 4.0 | Burns / Lightning / Electrocution | Stop the burning process, airway assessment, cover, maintain temperature |
| 4.4 | Musculoskeletal Injuries | Splint including traction splints, assess circulation before and after |
| 4.5 | Spinal Motion Restriction | Apply when the spinal assessment algorithm requires it |
| 5.0 | Airway Management Guideline | Positioning, suction, OPA and NPA, BVM |
| 5.3 | CPAP / BiPAP | **CPAP is the only approved adjunct for BLS**; indications, contraindications and `5-10 cm H2O` pressure range as printed |
| 6.0 | Spinal Assessment | The algorithm that decides whether motion restriction is required |
| 6.5 | Restraints | No hard restraints unless the applying officer accompanies the patient; never prone; document reason, type, time, circulation checks, injuries |

> **Key:** If a protocol has no EMT block, there is nothing in it for you to perform. Read it anyway, so you can set the medic up.
